facts.fact: In a presentation of 18 July 2026 the Civil Registry Department states it is implementing a secure interoperability platform to exchange birth and death notifications with the Ministry of Health and Child Care, with API/middleware design due Q4 2026 and a three-province pilot in Q1-Q2 2027.

systems.owner: Civil Registry Department; Ministry of Health and Child Care

facts.fact: UNDP Zimbabwe published a request for proposals, UNDP-ZWE-01688, for technical assistance to develop a Health Information Exchange Platform, with a deadline of 22 June 2026; the public notice gives no scope.

A DHIS2 community post says Impilo EHR, deployed across over 700 facilities, sends data to DHIS2 using FHIR, by real-time OpenHIE pipeline for connected facilities, reporting over 150 indicators and 15 facility registers; as_of is the post's published date.

facts.fact: DHIS2.org says the Ministry of Health and Child Care, with Global Fund support, is integrating the case-based surveillance system with the NHIS so patient data flows as anonymised indicators in near real time; in June 2026 it was in final testing with go-live expected by end July 2026.

UNDP Zimbabwe published request for proposal UNDP-ZWE-02187 on 13 November 2026 for technical assistance to design the Health Information Exchange architecture, core platform configuration, mediators and secure channels.
